text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena said on Wednesday it was still aiming for a return to profitability in 1998.

The cooperation with Swissair, Delta Airlines, Austrian Airlines, Virgin Express, Finnair and Tyrolean was strengthened and should show its full effect from 1997, it said. It added that synergies with Swissair would yield 600 million Belgian francs for Sabena in 1997.
Sabena said in a statement the results of synergies in general would continue to improve as the collaboration with various companies within the Swissair group increased.
"The above developments, which all derive from a radical company restructuring, should provide a firm foundation for restoring Sabena to profitability in 1998," it said.
Initial results for 1997 suggested that traffic was picking up well, it said. Figures showed a 17 percent improvement compared with the same period last year.
Sabena is 49.5 percent owned by Swissair.
